item.title: Split the difference
item.description:
Splitting the difference between two opposing views often seems clever. “Those darn’d hardliners! I’m a centrist!”

On software teams, there are often disputes between those who want a quality solution and those who just want to ship. For a manager here, splitting the difference between the two can seem like a great option. Maintaining this stance makes one seem a pragmatist in a sea of idealists. Since neither party gets their way, it can allow a manager to seem fair and impartial.

item.title: Idiomatic Code
item.description:
You can call it “beautiful code” when the code also makes it look like the language was made for the problem - Ward Cunningham

If you have a sound continuous integration practice, your pull requests will be automatically evaluated for test coverage and compliance with code conventions. But it’s your teammates who will evaluate the degree to which the submitted code is high quality through being idiomatic. What does this mean?
